Do NOT read lib/agent.ts's SYSTEM prompt in full, do NOT read lib/foundation.ts, lib/credits.ts, or lib/stripe.ts in detail — I am reading those myself. (You may grep them for specific facts if needed.)

2	//
3	// Kodely's #1 existential risk is unit economics (the LLM "token tax"), so the
4	// model choice is a product decision, not a default: Sonnet 5 is the codegen
5	// workhorse and Opus 5 is available for planning / hard repairs. Both are
6	// overridable per-environment so we can retune without a code change.
7	
8	// Why Sonnet 5 and not Opus 5: on coding and agentic work Sonnet 5 lands close
9	// enough to Opus that the difference does not show up in a static marketing
10	// site, while costing $3/$15 per MTok against Opus 5's $5/$25. Haiku 4.5 is
11	// cheaper still but design quality is the product, so that is the wrong saving.
12	export const MODELS = {
13	  /** Writes and edits the site. Handles the overwhelming majority of builds. */
14	  builder: process.env.KODELY_MODEL_BUILDER ?? "claude-sonnet-5",
15	  /** Reserved for planning and repair of builds the workhorse couldn't fix. */
16	  planner: process.env.KODELY_MODEL_PLANNER ?? "claude-opus-5",
17	  /**
18	   * Expands a one-line prompt into an editable spec (lib/enhance.ts). This is
19	   * a few hundred words of prose, not code and not a design problem, so the
20	   * "design quality is the product" argument for Sonnet does not apply — Haiku
21	   * is a third of the price and the user edits the result anyway. Enhance is
22	   * also unbilled, so it comes straight off margin: the cheap model is the
23	   * only one that makes the feature free to offer.
24	   */
25	  enhancer: process.env.KODELY_MODEL_ENHANCER ?? "claude-haiku-4-5",
26	} as const;
27	
28	// Effort moves spend more than the model choice does — Sonnet 5 at `medium` is
29	// roughly Sonnet 4.6 at `high`. A blank-page first build is a genuine design
30	// problem and earns `high`; a targeted tweak does not.
31	export const EFFORT = {
32	  create: (process.env.KODELY_EFFORT_CREATE ?? "high") as "high",
33	  edit: (process.env.KODELY_EFFORT_EDIT ?? "medium") as "medium",
34	} as const;

36	/** USD per million tokens. Used to meter real spend per build. */

42	  "claude-sonnet-5": { input: 3, output: 15, cacheRead: 0.3, cacheWrite: 3.75 },
43	  "claude-haiku-4-5": { input: 1, output: 5, cacheRead: 0.1, cacheWrite: 1.25 },

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# deploy.sh — push this checkout's committed work to kodely.me.
#
#   ./deploy.sh            staging -> verify -> prod -> verify
#   ./deploy.sh --staging  stop after staging
#
# Transport note: the VM cannot currently reach GitHub over SSH (see the board
# card "VM cannot reach GitHub over SSH"). Its own /home/kodely/deploy.sh runs
# `git fetch origin main && git reset --hard origin/main`, and when that fetch
# fails it resets to a STALE remote-tracking ref and reports a healthy deploy
# of the WRONG commit — it did that twice on 2026-08-21.
#
# So this script does not rely on the VM pulling. It still pushes to GitHub
# (that works from here, and keeps origin authoritative), then ships the actual
# commits over the existing SSH path as a git bundle and builds in place. When
# the VM's GitHub access is restored, the bundle step can be dropped.
set -euo pipefail

HOST=root@51.79.162.96
VM=kodely@10.20.0.30
STAGING_ONLY="${1:-}"

say() { printf '\n\033[1m== %s\033[0m\n' "$*"; }
die() { printf '\n\033[31mABORT: %s\033[0m\n' "$*" >&2; exit 1; }
vm()  { ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=15 "$HOST" "ssh -o BatchMode=yes $VM \"$1\""; }

say "Pre-flight"
[ "$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)" = "main" ] || die "not on main"
[ -z "$(git status --porcelain)" ] || die "working tree dirty — commit first"

git fetch -q origin main || die "cannot reach GitHub from here"
if [ -n "$(git log --oneline origin/main..HEAD)" ]; then
  say "Pushing to origin/main"
  git log --oneline origin/main..HEAD | sed 's/^/  /'
  git push -q origin main
fi
NEW=$(git rev-parse --short HEAD)
echo "  main = $NEW"

ROLLBACK=$(vm 'cd /opt/kodely && git rev-parse --short HEAD')
say "Rollback point (current prod): $ROLLBACK"

# --------------------------------------------------------------- transport
# Bundle only what the VM is missing, using prod's current HEAD as the base.
say "Bundling commits for the VM"
# Base on the OLDER of the two environments, not just prod: staging is
# routinely behind, and a bundle cut from prod's HEAD would be missing the
# commits staging still needs. merge-base gives the common ancestor.
PROD_HEAD=$(vm 'cd /opt/kodely && git rev-parse HEAD')
STAGING_HEAD=$(vm 'cd /opt/kodely-staging && git rev-parse HEAD')
for c in "$PROD_HEAD" "$STAGING_HEAD"; do
  git cat-file -e "${c}^{commit}" 2>/dev/null || die "the VM is on commit ${c:0:7}, which this checkout does not have — fetch/rebase first"
done
BASE=$(git merge-base "$PROD_HEAD" "$STAGING_HEAD")
echo "  prod=${PROD_HEAD:0:7}  staging=${STAGING_HEAD:0:7}  base=${BASE:0:7}"

if [ "$BASE" = "$(git rev-parse HEAD)" ]; then
  echo "  both environments already at $NEW — nothing to transport"
  rm -f /tmp/kodely-deploy.bundle
  vm "rm -f /tmp/kodely-deploy.bundle" || true

What Kodely Cannot Build Yet The complete, blunt list of what Kodely cannot do today � no backend, no forms that deliver, no photos, no multi-page routing. Read before signing up.

This page exists so that nobody signs up expecting something that isn't there. Everything below is a real limitation today, written plainly rather than softened. If one of these is a dealbreaker for you, we'd rather you found out here than after you'd spent an afternoon.

No backend of any kind

A Kodely site is a front end. There is no server code, no database, no API layer, no scheduled jobs, no email sending. Nothing your visitors do on the page is stored or transmitted anywhere.

That single fact is upstream of most of what follows.

No contact forms that deliver

A form on a generated site would collect a message and have nowhere to send it. If you ask for one you may well get a well-designed form that silently discards every enquiry � so don't ask for one.

What to do instead: link out. An email address as a mailto: link, a phone number as a tel: link, or a button pointing at whatever tool you already use. Links are ordinary navigations, so they work normally � the restriction is on what the page can load, not where it can send someone.

No user accounts, logins, or member areas

No sign-up, no sign-in, no password reset, no dashboard, no admin panel, no gated content. All of it needs somewhere to store a user, and there is nowhere.

A login screen can be drawn as a visual element. It won't authenticate anyone. Don't ship one.

No e-commerce, carts, checkout, or payments

You cannot sell anything from a Kodely site. No cart, no checkout, no payment processor, no order records, no inventory.

What to do instead: a product page that describes what you sell, with a button linking out to the store, marketplace or payment link you already have.

No bookings or reservations that reserve anything

Same reason. A date picker can exist as a visual element and it will hold nothing. Link out to your booking platform, or make the phone number a large tap-to-call button.

No external API integrations

Published sites run under a content security policy that switches off the page's ability to make outbound network requests entirely. So no live prices, no weather, no currency conversion, no CRM sync, no email-list signup posting to a provider, no chat widget, no analytics.

No images, photography, or remote media

No stock photos, no image search, no photo uploads today, no remote images of any kind, no embedded maps, no video embeds, no social feeds. Every request to another host is blocked.

Everything visual is drawn by the page itself: inline SVG, CSS gradients, colour and typography. If your site's whole job is showing photographs � a photographer's portfolio, property listings, a lookbook � this is the wrong tool today, straightforwardly. The full reasoning is here.

No custom web fonts

Not from a font service, and not embedded in the page either � a base64-encoded font is blocked by the same policy as a remote one. Sites use the system font stack. It's fast and it renders instantly, but it is a genuine limit on brand expression.

No multi-page routing

Kodely builds single-page sites. Sections are things you scroll to, not separate URLs. There is no /about, no /services/plumbing, no blog with individual post pages.

For most small business sites this is fine and arguably better. If your plan depends on ranking twenty separate service pages for twenty separate search terms, it isn't. The trade-off, in detail.

No npm packages

Generated projects have exactly two runtime dependencies: React and React DOM. No animation library, no carousel, no icon package, no charting library, no date picker, no form library, no router. There's no install step during generation, so there's no mechanism to add one.

Anything you'd normally reach for a package to do has to be written from scratch in the project's own components � which is fine for a fade-in or an accordion, and genuinely limiting for something like a full data grid.

No custom domains

Published sites live on a kodely.site subdomain. You can't point your own domain at a Kodely-hosted site today. If you need your own domain now, download your source as a zip � it's a standard Vite project � and host it wherever you like.

No content management for non-technical editors

There's no CMS, no editable-region UI, no way to hand a member of staff a login so they can change the menu. Edits happen by asking for them in the chat box, which requires access to your Kodely account and costs credits.

What you get in exchange

Being clear about the limits is only half of it. Here's the other half, and each of these is a consequence of the same design:

  • A real Vite + React + TypeScript + Tailwind project you can read and download, not a proprietary page format.
  • Every build genuinely compiled server-side, so type errors and broken markup are caught by a machine before you see the page.
  • Zero charge for a build that fails to compile.
  • Every successful build kept as a checkpoint you can roll back to for free.
  • A published site with no third-party requests at all � nothing to break when someone else's CDN changes, and no third-party tracking on your visitors.

So who is this actually for?

Kodely is a good fit if you need one well-built, fast, honest page: a local service business, a restaurant, a landing page for something you're launching, a text-led portfolio, an event, a one-page pitch for a product.

It's the wrong fit if you need a store, a booking system, logins, a photo-driven site, or twenty indexable pages. Those aren't things we're going to talk you into doing badly.

If you're in the first group: 750 free credits, no card required.

takeover:

- `connect-src 'none'` blocks `fetch`/`XHR`, so the script cannot call `/api/*` with the

# Kodely — Factual Capability Map (`C:\Users\edmem\kodely-prod`)

Read-only exploration. Nothing modified. All paths absolute; line numbers from the current tree.

---

## 1. AUTH & ACCOUNTS

**`C:\Users\edmem\kodely-prod\lib\auth.ts`** (91 lines) — hand-rolled, no NextAuth/Auth.js.

- Password hashing: `scrypt` from `node:crypto`, 16-byte random salt, 64-byte key, stored as `scrypt$<saltHex>$<keyHex>` (lines 15–28). Verify uses `timingSafeEqual` (line 27).
- Sessions: opaque random 32-byte `base64url` token (line 36), **SHA-256 hashed before storage** (lines 31–33, 38). Cookie `kodely_session`, `httpOnly`, `sameSite: "lax"`, `secure` in prod, `path: "/"`, **30-day** expiry (`SESSION_DAYS = 13`… actually line 13: `SESSION_DAYS = 30`), lines 12–13, 40–47. No `domain` attribute — deliberately host-only (referenced in `proxy.ts:51-57`).
- `getCurrentUser()` (57), `requireUser()` (70, throws `"UNAUTHENTICATED"`), `getAdminUser()` (87, role === `"ADMIN"`).
- **No JWT, no refresh tokens, no MFA, no CSRF token** (relies on `SameSite=Lax` + JSON-body parsing).

**Routes** under `C:\Users\edmem\kodely-prod\app\api\auth\`:

| Route | File | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /api/auth/signup` | `signup\route.ts` | email regex `EMAIL_RE` (line 9), password **min 8 chars only** (line 22). Grants `SIGNUP_GRANT` credits + `createSeedProject()` (36–37). **No email verification, no rate limit.** |
| `POST /api/auth/login` | `login\route.ts` | 28 lines. Constant-shape error (line 23). **No rate limit / lockout.** |
| `POST /api/auth/logout` | `logout\route.ts` | |
| `GET /api/auth/me` | `me\route.ts` | |
| `GET /api/auth/google/start` | `google\start\route.ts` | Manual OAuth2 (no library). Scope `openid email profile` (line 39). State cookie `kodely_google_oauth_state`, HttpOnly, 600s. **Inert without `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`** → redirects `/login?error=google_not_configured` (line 31). |
| `GET /api/auth/google/callback` | `google\callback\route.ts` | Code exchange → `openidconnect.googleapis.com/v1/userinfo`. Requires `email_verified` (line 68). Links Google to an existing email account by email (lines 76–79) rather than duplicating. |

**MISSING: no password reset / forgot-password flow anywhere** (`grep reset|forgot` over `app/(auth)/` and `app/api/auth/` returns nothing). No email verification. No account-deletion self-serve endpoint in auth (project delete exists; account deletion is a manual `mailto:privacy@kodely.me` per `app\legal\privacy\page.tsx:319`).

### `C:\Users\edmem\kodely-prod\prisma\schema.prisma` (307 lines, PostgreSQL)

13 models:

1. **User** (16) — `id`, `email` @unique, `passwordHash?` (nullable for Google-only), `googleId?` @unique, `name?`, `role` default `"CUSTOMER"` (`CUSTOMER|ADMIN`), `stripeCustomerId?`, `createdAt`, **`spendCapCredits Int?`** (user-set 30-day ceiling, line 32).

3. **EmailLog** (77) — `kind`, `dedupeKey`, `@@unique([kind, dedupeKey])` = exactly-once notification guard.
4. **AdminAuditLog** (92) — `actorId`, `actorEmail`, `action`, `targetType/Id`, `meta`.

7. **SupportNote** (153).
8. **StripeEvent** (168) — webhook idempotency, keyed by Stripe event id.
9. **Session** (174) — `tokenHash` @unique, `expiresAt`.

**First-party, self-hosted on an OVH VPS. No Vercel/Netlify/Cloudflare Pages deploy path exists.**

Explicit comment lines 12–15: *"Deliberately NOT deploying to real Nxeon hosting infra in Phase 1 … `*.kodely.site` is served straight out of this app from the published rows."*
  - Gates before publishing: new-subdomain rate limit (42–50), `scanForSecrets` (63–70), `moderateForPublish` + `blockingFindings` — only `high` severity blocks (80–95).
- **Published URL shape** (`publish\route.ts:132-136`):
  - prod: `https://<slug>.kodely.site`
  - staging (Host contains "staging"): `https://<host>/api/site/<slug>`
  - Slug generated at project creation: `slugify(name).slice(0,40) + "-" + 5 random base36 chars` (`app\api\projects\route.ts:8-15`).

**CUSTOM DOMAINS: NOT SUPPORTED.** No `domain`/`cname` field in the schema, no route, no UI. The product's own SEO content states it explicitly — `C:\Users\edmem\kodely-prod\content\seo\what-kodely-cannot-build-yet.json:47-48` ("No custom domains… You can't point your own domain at a Kodely-hosted site today") and `content\seo\publishing-and-indexing-an-ai-built-site.json:29`. No `vercel`/`netlify` reference anywhere in `lib/` or `app/`.

---

## 3. THE SANDBOX / CSP

**Exact header, published sites** — `C:\Users\edmem\kodely-prod\app\api\site\[slug]\[[...path]]\route.ts:28-29`:

```
default-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data:; connect-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'self'
```

**Exact header, previews** — `C:\Users\edmem\kodely-prod\app\api\preview\[id]\[[...path]]\route.ts:16-17`: **byte-identical string** (two independent copies; no shared constant).

What that actually blocks:

- **All external hosts**: `default-src 'self'` — no remote images, fonts, scripts, stylesheets, iframes, media, no map/video/social embeds.
- **All outbound network calls from the page**: `connect-src 'none'` — `fetch`, `XHR`, `WebSocket`, `EventSource`, `sendBeacon` all dead. No analytics, no API integrations, no live data.
- **Images**: `'self'` + `data:` only. Inline SVG and data-URI images work; `blob:` does not.
- **Fonts**: no `font-src`, so it falls back to `default-src 'self'`. A remote webfont is blocked, **and so is a base64/`data:` embedded font** (documented at `content\seo\what-kodely-cannot-build-yet.json` "No custom web fonts").
- **Scripts DO run**: `script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'` — the compiled Vite bundle plus inline scripts execute. React runs normally.
- **Styles**: `'self' 'unsafe-inline'` — Tailwind output + inline styles fine.
- `frame-ancestors 'self'` — the app's own editor iframe can embed it.

**Known gaps, documented in-repo:**
- `C:\Users\edmem\kodely-prod\docs\security\audit-2026-08.md:29` (M4) — **`form-action` and `base-uri` are omitted**, so a generated page can `POST` a form to any external host, and links/navigations are unrestricted.

## Bottom line: CAN vs CANNOT

**CAN**: email/password + Google sign-in; generate a real compiled Vite+React+TS+Tailwind single-page site from a prompt (or a reference image for style); one automatic repair pass when the build doesn't compile; conversationally edit an existing site with full history; free rollback to any successful build; responsive preview at 3 widths; publish to `<slug>.kodely.site` served from Postgres with auto robots.txt/sitemap.xml/SEO backstop; download the full source as a .zip (no gating); 23 starter prompts; ~460 inlinable icons/flags/gradients/patterns; credit ledger + Stripe top-ups + user-set spend cap; free-build-on-failure; secret scan and heuristic abuse moderation at publish; admin panel, audit log, analytics, transactional email, social rewards.

**CANNOT**: custom domains; multi-page/routing; any backend, form delivery, auth, cart, or payments in a generated site; any external network request from a generated page (`connect-src 'none'`); remote or uploaded images, stock photos, embeds, maps, video, custom web fonts (incl. data-URI fonts); npm packages beyond react/react-dom; password reset or email verification for Kodely accounts; CMS/non-technical editing; in-editor code editing (code view is read-only `<pre>`); analytics on published sites.

**Built but not wired**: `GET /api/assets` (no UI consumes it); `lib/flags.ts` kill switches (`isEnabled` never called from product code); `MODELS.planner` (`claude-opus-5`, never routed to); `lib/retention.ts` (no scheduler invoking it).
